findings.title: Security audit M1: HttpRequestUtils.extractIp trusts X-Forwarded-For without proxy allowlist
findings.expected: X-Forwarded-For parsed only when request originates from a known proxy IP, OR the application is fronted by a reverse proxy that overwrites the header.
findings.actual: backend/src/main/java/com/botfunnel/common/HttpRequestUtils.java:33 reads X-Forwarded-For unconditionally. An external client can spoof it and rotate the IP key on every login attempt, evading the brute-force counter. Pre-existing pre-migration semantic — preserved through the migration touch surface (not introduced by this work).
findings.reproduction: Send POST /api/auth/login with `X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.42` from any client; observe the brute counter increments against 10.0.0.42, not the real source IP.
findings.impact: Per-IP brute-force defence collapses to per-spoofed-header counter. Same vector for register-storm + forgot-password-flood. OWASP A07 / CWE-348. Remediation: deploy behind nginx/traefik that overwrites the header (inline Javadoc already states this is the production contract), OR add app.trusted-proxies allowlist with IP check. Tracking on deployment-story backlog.

findings.title: Security audit M2: Hardcoded weak defaults BOT_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY (0x00 ×32) and SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD ("12345678") in application.properties
findings.expected: Defaults are empty strings; fail-secure paths in TokenEncryptor (throws IllegalStateException on blank) and SuperAdminSeeder (short-circuit + WARN on blank) already exist and would refuse to boot the app or seed the super-admin.
findings.actual: backend/src/main/resources/application.properties:41 default BOT_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY is 64 zero hex chars (32 zero bytes). Line 47 default SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD is `12345678`. If env vars are forgotten in production, every persisted bot token is decryptable with a publicly-known constant AND admin@admin.com is seeded with the textbook default password.
findings.impact: OWASP A02 + A05; CWE-798 + CWE-1188. Trivial admin takeover or trivial decryption of persisted tokens if either env var unset. Fail-secure plumbing already exists — only the defaults need to flip to empty. Pre-existing, not introduced by this migration.

findings.title: Security audit M3: CSRF handler is plain CsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler instead of XOR (Task 15 spec demands XOR for BREACH mitigation)
findings.expected: XorCsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler per Task 15 description — masks the form-attribute token per request to break BREACH oracles on compressed response bodies.
findings.actual: backend/src/main/java/com/botfunnel/security/SecurityConfig.java:75 uses plain CsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler. Inline Javadoc justifies the choice (no compressible JSON body renders the token; XOR would break the cookie/header round-trip with CookieCsrfTokenRepository). The architecture is BREACH-safe by construction, but spec and code diverge.
findings.reproduction: Open backend/src/main/java/com/botfunnel/security/SecurityConfig.java:67-80; compare against tech-spec.md Task 15 description.
findings.impact: Not a runtime vulnerability in the chosen architecture. The Medium is for the spec-vs-code divergence — should resolve explicitly by either updating tech-spec Task 15 to document the no-BREACH-because-no-body-render argument, OR switching to XorCsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler with `handler.setCsrfRequestAttributeName(null)` so cookie/header uses raw token + form-binding uses masked.

findings.title: Security audit L1: TC11 XSRF-TOKEN co-emission on the SAME login response not asserted in test suite
findings.expected: End-to-end real-Tomcat IT: (a) GET /health primes XSRF-TOKEN cookie; (b) POST /api/auth/login with cookie + X-XSRF-TOKEN; (c) assert login response carries BOTH SESSION and XSRF-TOKEN Set-Cookie.
findings.actual: AuthControllerIT.java:603-615 javadoc documents the limitation — with `.with(csrf())` the test post-processor substitutes TestCsrfTokenRepository; without it the POST returns 403. CookieCsrfTokenRepository.saveToken is never reached in test. CsrfMaterializerIT.csrfCookie_writtenOnSafeVerbRequest covers the safe-verb fresh-GET path only, AND is itself broken under full-suite run (critical finding above).
findings.reproduction: Read AuthControllerIT.java:591-650 docstring, then look at CsrfMaterializerIT failure in qa-evidence/test-default.txt.
findings.impact: TC11 invariant not pinned at IT level. A regression that deletes CsrfCookieMaterializer would silently break SPA's first-POST-after-login flow. Remediation: extend BotConnectRaceIT.login real-Tomcat round-trip to add the (c) assertion.

findings.actual: ProcessTelegramUpdateJobTest:487-489 uses appender-wide negative assertion (`jobAppender.list ... allSatisfy(e -> token_regex_does_not_match)`); covers the negative case generically but does not lock that EACH of the 4 ProcessTelegramUpdateJob log sites has a scrubber on its arguments.

findings.impact: A scrubber regression on a specific site could survive the test suite if fixtures don't inject a token-shaped string at THAT site. Track in Task 16 follow-ups.

findings.title: Security audit L5: 3 ProcessTelegramUpdateJob log sites pass unscrubbed string arguments
findings.expected: All payload-derived args wrapped in TelegramApiClient.scrubTokens(...) even when current arg shape (Mongo ObjectId / Long) cannot match the token regex — defence-in-depth typing constraint.
findings.actual: ProcessTelegramUpdateJob.java lines 96-97, 107-108, 211-212 pass raw rawUpdateId / projectId / chatId. Cannot leak today (shape mismatch with `\d{1,20}:[A-Za-z0-9_-]{30,50}` regex).
